clue.text: Singer reportedly used to engage in casual talk

indicators.note: reportedly means we only hear the phrase said, so its sound is entered, not its spelling

parts.words: used to engage in casual talk
parts.note: 'would chat' is the habitual past: someone who used to chat would chat

explanation.surface: A vocalist who once enjoyed a bit of idle gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a human vocalist, but it is a songbird; the rest, spoken, gives 'would chat'.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodchat shrike is a small European bird, and birds that sing are crossword singers.

clue.text: Fast woman initially one of the flower people

indicators.note: initially takes only the opening letter of woman

parts.note: the hippies of the 1960s were called flower people

explanation.surface: A promiscuous woman who was a hippie in the 1960s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast woman' reads as a loose one, but 'Fast' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Whippy can mean quick and lively, nimble as a whip's crack.

clue.text: Passable actor going round a one-time king's hiding-place

parts.note: OK means passable, satisfactory

explanation.surface: A mediocre actor touring round the hiding place of a former monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles II hid in an oak at Boscobel after the Battle of Worcester in 1651.
explanation.definitionFit: The future Charles II escaped Cromwell's soldiers by concealing himself in the Royal Oak.

clue.text: Baddie's extremely useful vessel given position in Rome once

parts.note: a ship is a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: The consulship was the office of consul, one of the two chief magistrates of the Roman Republic.

clue.text: Children's author's legendary king, free at last after pay-off

explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons, a classic of British children's fiction.

clue.text: Eg kitchen utensils wife kept in safe

explanation.walkthrough: PETER for a safe is old underworld slang, as in a safe-breaker called a peterman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pewter also names articles made of that tin alloy collectively, such as plates, tankards and kitchenware.

clue.text: Lamb a priest served as starter?

clue.text: Time a girl put away salt

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.definitionFit: A tannate is a chemical salt of tannic acid.

clue.text: Motor sport competitor's sidekick lives in outskirts of Rabat

clue.text: Writing-fluid half-hearted leftist has abandoned quietly

clue.text: Travelling in Turin a lot, providing food and nourishment

explanation.definitionFit: Insubordinate describes someone defying authority, disobedient to superiors.

clue.text: Language left university visitor briefly embarrassed at first

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

indicators.note: briefly cuts the visitor word short, dropping its final letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims the final T from GUEST.

clue.text: Like light mist unknown in market town on Wye

explanation.walkthrough: Hay-on-Wye is a small town on the Welsh border, known for its book festival.

clue.text: Society leaving Waugh's country house without good fortification

explanation.walkthrough: Removing S gives BRIDEHEAD; 'without' means outside, so it goes round G.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a fortified position held on the enemy side of a river.

clue.text: Water heater, nasty grey, seen around Home Counties

nasty suggests the letters of grey made foul and jumbled

explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a geyser is a gas appliance that heats water on demand, as well as a hot spring.

clue.text: Bishop presses son to become freeman of borough

S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

clue.text: Tropical plant better thus? Let me think

um is the sound of someone pausing to think

clue.text: Asian heretic inspiring a book

clue.text: Equestrian pursuit in part of Yorkshire once

second meaning: Yorkshire was formerly divided into three ..., North, East and West

clue.text: Element of Northern Ireland I instilled in old tramp

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant

clue.text: Way you and I knocked back olla podrida, say?

parts.note: you and I together are we

explanation.walkthrough: Olla podrida is a Spanish meat and vegetable dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Olla podrida is a slow-cooked Spanish casserole, an example of a hearty pot dish; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Like some trees in course of being cultivated

clue.text: Displaying solicitude, study team standard

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a side is a sports team
a rate is a standard, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A careful report rating a team's level of care.

clue.text: Call during play originally mounted by French department
